On Tue, May 12, 2026 at 10:02 AM kimberly_park wrote:
> Team — forwarding FinBank's redlines...

I reviewed their redline and prepared a clean counter with rationale. Main points:
1) Retention: their proposed hard-delete on request for all aggregated data conflicts with existing platform cache/metrics retention. Propose a middle path: make-specified categories deletable on request and offer a separate retention SLO for aggregated telemetry used for performance.
2) UK IDTA: we can accept an Annex B style addendum with minimal edits. We'll map our SCCs implementation details into a short UK addendum (we should confirm whether they want the standalone UK IDTA or an addendum tied to SCCs).
3) Subprocessors: we will provide the live CSV and a 30-day notice for new subprocessors; cannot accept blanket prior-approval requirement.
4) Liability cap: suggest Redwood's standard cap (monthly revenue x 12). Non-starter to their proposed open-ended indemnity.

I've attached our annotated counter (redline_dpa_finbank_v3.pdf) and a suggested Annex B text snippet that maps to our implementation.

If Sales is okay with the cap and the 30-day notice language, I can push the counter to them today.

-Rishi

Attachments: redline_dpa_finbank_v3.pdf; AnnexB_text_snippet.txt

Hi Ellie — thanks for the redlines and the tight timeline. Apologies for the delay — attaching our counter with annotations.

Short summary of the counter:
- We accept an Annex B (UK IDTA style) tied to SCCs; we included the implementation details and a note that the UK addendum applies only if FinBank has UK-resident data processing needs.
- Retention: we revised to allow deletion of personal records on request (subject to technical constraints for aggregated metrics and cached inference KV which we will purge within 30 days where applicable).
- Subprocessors: live list attached (subprocessor_list_may2026.csv); we provide 30-day notice for new subprocessors and emergency disclosures if a new subprocessor is required for security/availability.
- Execution: we can send via DocuSign or AdobeSign. Which e-sign provider does FinBank prefer? We can host the envelope and send for both signers.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the e-sign provider (DocuSign or AdobeSign) and who signs first (procurement or Redwood legal).
2) If FinBank accepts the counter, we'll create the envelope and share the TIA summary + SOC2 summary and subprocessor list as attachments.

I attached: redline_dpa_finbank_v3.pdf, subprocessor_list_may2026.csv, TIA_summary_finbank.pdf, SOC2-type2-summary-2025.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
